## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-7-trajectory-and-pseudotime-analysis-using-monocle-3/>

Part 2 of 3. The preprocessed CDS from part 1 is clustered into partitions
(groups of cells too different to be joined in one trajectory), a principal
graph is learned within each partition, and cells are ordered in pseudotime from
chosen roots. `learn_graph()` can take a while on several thousand cells.

**Pseudotime is only comparable within a partition**: each partition has its own
independent pseudotime scale.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 8-12). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)
library(SeuratWrappers)

# Trajectory inference
library(monocle3)

# Data manipulation and visualization
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
traj.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$traj.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots/trajectories", "plots/pseudotime", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(traj.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(traj.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names, condition levels and colors from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), unlist(params$condition.levels))
```

## Load objects from part 1

```{r step2_load_obj}
# ADDED: hand-off from part 1
cds <- readRDS(file.path(traj.dir, "results/cds_preprocessed.rds"))
cat("CDS: ", ncol(cds), " cells, ", nrow(cds), " genes\n", sep = "")
cat("Reductions:", names(reducedDims(cds)), "\n")
```

## Learn the trajectory graph structure

```{r step3_learn_graph}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: Cluster cells and learn principal graph
#-----------------------------------------------

# First, cluster cells (required before learn_graph)
# This identifies partitions and communities in the data
cds <- cluster_cells(
  cds,
  reduction_method = "UMAP",
  k = params$cluster.k,                      # Number of nearest neighbors
  cluster_method = params$cluster.method,    # Clustering algorithm
  num_iter = params$cluster.num_iter,        # Iterations for refinement
  partition_qval = params$cluster.partition_qval, # Significance threshold for partitions
  verbose = FALSE
)

cat("Number of partitions:", length(unique(partitions(cds))), "\n")
cat("Number of clusters:", length(unique(clusters(cds))), "\n\n")

# Now learn the trajectory graph structure
cds <- learn_graph(
  cds,
  use_partition = params$graph.use_partition, # Learn separate graphs per partition
  close_loop = params$graph.close_loop,       # Don't force circular trajectories
  learn_graph_control = list(
    ncenter = params$graph.ncenter,           # Number of centers for graph construction
    nn.k = params$graph.nn_k,                 # k-nearest neighbors
    prune_graph = params$graph.prune          # Remove spurious connections
  ),
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

## Handling multiple partitions

```{r step4_partitions}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: Analyze all partitions
#-----------------------------------------------

# Count cells per partition
partition_counts <- table(partitions(cds))
cat("Cells per partition:\n")
print(partition_counts)

# Identify which cell types are in each partition
cat("\nCell type distribution by partition:\n")
for (i in names(partition_counts)) {
  partition_cells <- colnames(cds)[partitions(cds) == i]
  cell_types_in_partition <- table(colData(cds)[[celltype.col]][partitions(cds) == i])
  cat("\nPartition", i, "(", partition_counts[[i]], "cells ):\n")
  print(cell_types_in_partition)
}

# Keep all partitions for complete analysis
cds_main <- cds

cat("\nRetaining all partitions for analysis:\n")
cat("  Total cells:", ncol(cds_main), "\n")
cat("  Total partitions:", length(unique(partitions(cds_main))), "\n")
cat("  Genes:", nrow(cds_main), "\n")
```

## Understanding pseudotime and root selection

Pseudotime is the distance along the trajectory from a chosen **root**. The root
should be a biologically justified starting state (e.g. a progenitor or naive
population); a wrong root reverses the direction of the trajectory without
changing its shape. Partitions that have no obvious biological starting
population can be given candidate cells, and Monocle 3 selects the root node.

The article orders each partition in turn (steps 10a-c), with CD4+ T cells as
the manual root of the T/NK partition and the first 50 cells as candidates in
the other partitions. Here the manual root is chosen by cell type
(`params$root.celltype`; its partition is the one containing most of those
cells), not by partition number, because partition numbering depends on the
clustering result.

### Step 10a: Partition with the manual root (CD4+ T cells in the article)

```{r step5_root_manual}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 10a: Order partition with manual root (CD4+ T cells)
#-----------------------------------------------

# ADDED: find the partition holding most cells of the root cell type (the
# article hard-codes partition 2 for this dataset)
all_partitions <- levels(factor(partitions(cds_main)))
root_ct_cells <- colData(cds_main)[[celltype.col]] == params$root.celltype
stopifnot(any(root_ct_cells))
root_partition <- names(which.max(table(partitions(cds_main)[root_ct_cells])))
cat("Manual root cell type:", params$root.celltype, "-> partition", root_partition, "\n")

# Get all cells in this partition
cells_manual <- colnames(cds_main)[partitions(cds_main) == root_partition]

# Select the root cell type as root (biologically informed starting point)
root_cells_manual <- cells_manual[
  colData(cds_main)[[celltype.col]][partitions(cds_main) == root_partition] == params$root.celltype
]

cat("Partition", root_partition, "root cells (", params$root.celltype, "):",
    length(root_cells_manual), "\n")
```

### Steps 10b-c: Remaining partitions (automatic roots)

```{r step6_root_auto}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 10b/10c: Remaining partitions - automatic roots
#-----------------------------------------------

# Provide the first n cells of each partition as candidates - Monocle 3 picks
# the best starting point. NOTE: "first n cells" is simply column order, i.e.
# an arbitrary set of candidates, not a biological choice
other_partitions <- setdiff(all_partitions, root_partition)

root_cells_auto <- list()
for (p in other_partitions) {
  cells_p <- colnames(cds_main)[partitions(cds_main) == p]
  root_cells_auto[[p]] <- cells_p[1:min(params$auto.root.n, length(cells_p))]
  cat("Partition", p, "root candidates provided:", length(root_cells_auto[[p]]), "\n")
}
```

### Order cells

```{r step7_order_cells}
# FIX: the article calls order_cells() once per partition (10a, 10b, 10c).
# Each call recomputes pseudotime for the whole object from the root cells it
# is given, so a later call can overwrite the ordering of earlier partitions.
# All root sets are combined and order_cells() is called once.
cds_main <- order_cells(
  cds_main,
  root_cells = c(root_cells_manual, unlist(root_cells_auto, use.names = FALSE)),
  verbose = FALSE
)

for (p in all_partitions) {
  cat("Partition", p, "pseudotime range:",
      round(range(pseudotime(cds_main)[partitions(cds_main) == p], na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
}
```

### Verify all partitions are ordered

```{r step8_verify}
#-----------------------------------------------
# Verify pseudotime across all partitions
#-----------------------------------------------

cat("Cells with NA or infinite pseudotime:", sum(!is.finite(pseudotime(cds_main))), "\n\n")

cat("Summary by partition:\n")
for (i in all_partitions) {
  pt_range <- round(range(pseudotime(cds_main)[partitions(cds_main) == i], na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  n <- sum(partitions(cds_main) == i)
  cat("  Partition", i, "(", n, "cells ): pseudotime", pt_range[1], "to", pt_range[2], "\n")
}
```

If any partition shows `Inf` pseudotime, it did not receive a root; check
`root_cells_auto` above.

## Visualize trajectories across all partitions

```{r step9_trajectory_plots, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 12}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 11: Visualize trajectories and pseudotime
#-----------------------------------------------

# Plot 1: Trajectory colored by cell type
p_trajectory_celltype <- plot_cells(
  cds_main,
  color_cells_by = celltype.col,
  label_cell_groups = TRUE,
  label_groups_by_cluster = FALSE,
  label_leaves = FALSE,
  label_branch_points = FALSE,
  graph_label_size = 3,
  cell_size = 1
) +
  ggtitle("Trajectory Structure (Colored by Cell Type)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9))

# Plot 2: Trajectory colored by pseudotime
p_trajectory_pseudotime <- plot_cells(
  cds_main,
  color_cells_by = "pseudotime",
  label_cell_groups = FALSE,
  label_leaves = FALSE,
  label_branch_points = TRUE,
  label_roots = TRUE,
  graph_label_size = 4,
  cell_size = 1
) +
  scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma", name = "Pseudotime") +
  ggtitle("Trajectory Colored by Pseudotime") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# Plot 3: Trajectory colored by condition
p_trajectory_condition <- plot_cells(
  cds_main,
  color_cells_by = condition.col,
  label_cell_groups = FALSE,
  label_leaves = FALSE,
  label_branch_points = FALSE,
  cell_size = 1
) +
  scale_color_manual(values = condition.colors) +
  ggtitle("Trajectory Colored by Condition") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# Plot 4: Trajectory colored by partition (if multiple exist)
n_partitions <- length(unique(partitions(cds_main)))

if (n_partitions > 1) {
  p_trajectory_partition <- plot_cells(
    cds_main,
    color_cells_by = "partition",
    label_cell_groups = TRUE,
    label_groups_by_cluster = FALSE,
    label_leaves = FALSE,
    label_branch_points = FALSE,
    cell_size = 1
  ) +
    ggtitle("Trajectory Colored by Partition") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

  # Combine plots (4-panel)
  p_trajectory_overview <- (p_trajectory_celltype | p_trajectory_pseudotime) /
                           (p_trajectory_condition | p_trajectory_partition)
} else {
  # Combine plots (3-panel)
  p_trajectory_overview <- (p_trajectory_celltype | p_trajectory_pseudotime) /
                           (p_trajectory_condition | plot_spacer())
}
print(p_trajectory_overview)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/trajectories/02_trajectory_overview.png"),
       p_trajectory_overview, width = 16, height = 12, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Custom pseudotime visualizations

```{r step10_custom_plots, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 12: Custom pseudotime visualizations
#-----------------------------------------------

# Extract data for custom plotting
plot_data <- data.frame(
  UMAP_1 = reducedDims(cds_main)[["UMAP"]][,1],
  UMAP_2 = reducedDims(cds_main)[["UMAP"]][,2],
  pseudotime = pseudotime(cds_main),
  cell_type = colData(cds_main)[[celltype.col]],
  condition = colData(cds_main)[[condition.col]],
  sample = colData(cds_main)[[sample.col]],
  partition = factor(partitions(cds_main))
)

# Custom pseudotime plot with ggplot2
p_custom_pseudotime <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = UMAP_1, y = UMAP_2, color = pseudotime)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma", name = "Pseudotime") +
  labs(title = "Pseudotime Distribution Across All Partitions",
       x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "right")
print(p_custom_pseudotime)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/03_custom_pseudotime.png"),
       p_custom_pseudotime, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Pseudotime distribution by cell type (violin plot)
p_pseudotime_violin <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = reorder(cell_type, pseudotime, median),
                                              y = pseudotime, fill = cell_type)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, scale = "width", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Pseudotime Distribution by Cell Type",
       subtitle = "Note: Pseudotime not comparable across partitions",
       x = "Cell Type", y = "Pseudotime") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "none")
print(p_pseudotime_violin)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/04_pseudotime_by_celltype.png"),
       p_pseudotime_violin, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Pseudotime distribution by condition (density plot with facets for partitions)
n_partitions <- length(unique(plot_data$partition))

if (n_partitions > 1) {
  p_pseudotime_density <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = pseudotime, fill = condition)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ partition, ncol = 1,
               labeller = labeller(partition = function(x) paste("Partition", x))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = condition.colors) +
    labs(title = "Pseudotime Distribution by Condition (Per Partition)",
         subtitle = "Each partition has independent pseudotime scale",
         x = "Pseudotime", y = "Density", fill = "Condition") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
} else {
  p_pseudotime_density <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = pseudotime, fill = condition)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = condition.colors) +
    labs(title = "Pseudotime Distribution by Condition",
         x = "Pseudotime", y = "Density", fill = "Condition") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
}
print(p_pseudotime_density)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/05_pseudotime_by_condition.png"),
       p_pseudotime_density, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Additional plot: Partition-specific pseudotime (if multiple partitions)
if (n_partitions > 1) {
  # Create separate plots for each partition
  partition_plots <- list()

  for (i in levels(plot_data$partition)) {
    partition_data <- plot_data[plot_data$partition == i, ]
    cell_types_in_partition <- unique(partition_data$cell_type)

    partition_plots[[i]] <- ggplot(partition_data,
                                    aes(x = UMAP_1, y = UMAP_2, color = pseudotime)) +
      geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma", name = "Pseudotime") +
      labs(title = paste0("Partition ", i),
           subtitle = paste("Cell types:", paste(cell_types_in_partition, collapse = ", ")),
           x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") +
      theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
  }

  # Combine partition plots
  p_partition_combined <- wrap_plots(partition_plots, ncol = 2)
  print(p_partition_combined)

  ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/06_pseudotime_per_partition.png"),
         p_partition_combined, width = 14, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
}
```
